blueprint.context: Thecla Bram's last instruction to Pell in chapter 1 was to put a line in a hand coming north at the Ferry on day thirteen if there was one worth writing. There is a northbound crossing on the rock and it rolls at first light. Hanei was given the pound at Sixty Wells and told: if you are ever wrong, come and tell me you were wrong before somebody else tells me you were right.
objectives: Fire the gun Ana planted: a northbound crossing, a strip of paper two fingers wide, and a debt that has to be paid in something.
Keep Pell sympathetic and unrepentant in the specific way canon requires -- he does not experience it as treachery, and he is not wrong about the words he sold.
Show the leak as a debt: sixty-four blocks, a quarter's interest, and a daughter who goes on the paper at fourteen.
Put Hanei in the position of choosing her master over the man who has been kind to her, and let her tell in her own tell -- word for word.

setting.description: The Dry Ferry after dark: the walled pound with forty-one head watering in shifts off a stone trough, the jetty beyond it, and the northbound crossing's fires along the north side of the rock. Cut stone still giving back the day's heat through boot leather.

synopsis: Between shifts at the pound Hanei walks the jetty and finds Pell Corrow at the northbound crossing's fire with a girth across his knee, a borrowed pen and a strip of paper the width of two fingers. He does not hide it and he does not defend it; he explains it, and the explanation is worse. Hanei takes it to Ysoly, because Ysoly told her to, and Ysoly counts the butts and then sends for everybody.
title: Two Fingers Wide
